knowledge_gaps: Replacement items remain eligible candidates under the frozen original-prefix mask, potentially increasing top-ten overlap changes simply because inserted items become easy recommendations. Report effects with replacement identities excluded from a second, paired candidate set fixed across clean and altered histories.

Recent-versus-older sensitivity mixes recency with convolutional reachability, path structure and replacement plausibility. Frequency matching alone cannot isolate temporal preference or establish that stronger recency weighting would improve recommendations.

Reproduction requires explicit prefix sampling, lag-band boundaries, frequency-bin construction, replacement sampling and uniqueness rules, matching tolerances, intervention repetitions, and minimum coverage thresholds. Recent and older effects must use the same successfully matched prefixes.

User-bootstrap intervals from at most twelve users may be unstable and omit replacement randomness. Specify user-level weighting, paired contrast construction, bootstrap settings and uncertainty conditional on sampled corruptions.

Identity checks establish implementation consistency but do not calibrate diagnostic usefulness. Add controlled synthetic faults and dose-response checks, and bound catalog-scoring cost within the shared GPU budget.

Originality 5/10 is reasonable for an integration contribution. Potential 8/10 is speculative without evidence that these diagnostics guide successful repairs; difficulty 4/10 understates matching, calibration and uncertainty work. Near-zero mean embedding cosine also cannot rule out low-rank representation collapse.
